facts.text: The Microscope object holds a camera and a stage, and zeroes the stage backlash when it is created
close() shuts down the camera and the stage
rgb_image() captures a frame from the camera into a numpy array through picamera
freeze_camera_settings() turns off automatic exposure and white balance and sleeps around it

autofocus(dz, settle, metric_fn) moves the stage through the z positions in dz, sleeps settle seconds, captures an image at each and scores it with the sharpness metric, then moves back to the position with the highest score; it returns the positions and the scores
acquire_image_stack(step_displacement, n_steps, output_dir) captures one JPEG per scan point into output_dir
settings_dict() returns the camera attributes named in picamera_later_settings and picamera_init_settings: awb_mode, awb_gains, shutter_speed, brightness, contrast and resolution
settings_dict() is built from picamera_later_settings and picamera_init_settings
The zoom getter reports the scalar 2/(fov width + fov height) of the camera's zoom field of view: 1 means the whole sensor, more than 1 zooms in
The zoom setter raises a value below 1.0 to 1.0 and keeps the current image centre when it zooms
The upstream autofocus example builds dz in steps of 1000, 200, 100 and 50 and labels the position axis 'position (Microsteps)'
The clone ships a DummyStage stand-in for the stage and load_microscope(dummy_stage=True) uses it; the camera still has to be a real picamera
The interactive control offers zoom values 2**0 to 2**4 (1 to 16) and autofocus scans of 1280, 320 and 80 microsteps around the current position
The software runs the OpenFlexure Microscope: a Raspberry Pi camera and an OpenFlexure motor controller on a Raspberry Pi
The README says the camera module must be set up before use and the motor controller can be left out with --no_stage, which runs the camera without a motorised stage
